To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
systemic DOI administration increases Fos-immunostaining in GAD67-expressing cells in the dorsal raphe.
5-HT neurons of the dorsal DRN are subject to feedback inhibition by 5-HT2 activation and that the 5-HT feedback circuit involves GABA neurons in the dorsal DRN.
5-HT2 agonist-induced Fos immunoreactivity in the dorsal raphe was abolished by the selective 5-HT2 antagonist ritanserin, and was extensively colocalised in GAD67-positive neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of GABA in 5-HT homeostatic regulation
the mechanisms of action of 5-hydroxyltryptamine (serotonin; 5-HT) on 5-HT neurons of the dorsal and median raphe nucleus (RN).
the mechanisms by which 5-HT neurons of the dorsal and median raphe nuclei (DRN & MRN) are regulated by feedback from 5-HT receptors, and how such regulation may be altered in psychiatric disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
5-HT2 agonism activates GABA neurons in the dorsal raphe, and that the GABA neurons inhibit neighbouring 5HT neurons.
the 5-HT neurons of the dorsal and median raphe nuclei are subject to feedback inhibition by 5-HT2C receptors.
the 5-HT neurons in the DRN are subject to feedback inhibition from GABA neurons, and this feedback is mediated by 5-HT2(A) receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
5-HT2 agonism activates DRNA GABA neurons, which inhibit 5-HT neurons via local axonal collaterals.
5-HT2 agonism activates GABAergic DRN neurons that inhibit 5-HT neurons and that these GABAergic neurons may be involved in 5-HT negative feedback control.
the DRN is a heterogeneous structure with respect to its GABAergic neurons, and the GABAergic neurons are heterogeneous with respect to their neurotransmitter phenotype.
The main takeaway from our work is that
5-HT2 agonism increases the activity of GABA neurons in the midbrain raphe.
5-HT2-mediated feedback control of 5-HT neurons in the DRN is likely to be exerted through GABAergic interneurons.
the GABA system plays an important role in the feedback control of 5-HT neurons.
